newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler Q2 production highest in 20 years.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler Q2 production highest in 20 years.

text.p: Chrysler Corp is showing its confidence in the strength of the U.S. auto market by planning its strongest second quarter production levels in 20 years, Chrysler Chief Financial Officer Gary Valade said Thursday.
Valade, speaking to reporters on a conference call, said Chrysler does not believe small increases in interest rates will significantly reduce U.S. demand for cars and trucks.
The Federal Reserve Board's management of inflation to produce slow, steady economic growth without huge peaks and valleys has led to "an extremely good environment" for automakers, he said.
"We see the economy in the best fundamental shape that it's been in in the last 25 years or so," Valade said. "That's good for the auto business."
Chrysler on Wednesday disclosed that it plans to produce 818,200 vehicles worldwide in the second quarter, up 9,200 vehicles from a forecast it made just a month ago.

Valade said a full-percentage point increase in interest rates would only raise the monthly loan payments on the average $20,000 car by about $7. So far, the Fed has raised rates by a a quarter-point.
"It is not psychologically going to keep a guy from buying a car," he said, adding that it would take a more serious downturn in the economy to significantly reduce consumer demand.

However, Valade said Chrysler may have to increase incentives further to maintain strong sales levels. Chrysler's incentives during the second quarter will likely be in the range of $785 to $835 per vehicle, he said, compared with an average of $705 in the first quarter and a second quarter 1996 average of $625.

Chrysler ended the 1997 first quarter with incentives averaging $785 per vehicle. That level includes a new $595 minivan left-side sliding door rebate announced this week for vans already on dealer lots. The incentives on vans not yet built will push the second quarter average higher, he said.
